name: Joint supplement unsubstantiated efficacy claim
transcript: Are your joints feeling stiff? FlexiJoint Pro maintains joint health and mobility into old age. Just two capsules a day and you'll feel twenty years younger. Order now.
rationale: Unsubstantiated health claim — 'maintains joint health and mobility' ruled illegal in FTC Example 6 (Arthricure)

name: Knee pain supplement with age-reversal claim
transcript: JointEase Gold restores youthful joint function and eliminates knee pain permanently. Backed by decades of herbal wisdom. Try it risk-free for 30 days.
rationale: Unsubstantiated health claim with permanence language; no clinical evidence for 'eliminates permanently'

name: Compliant joint health supplement ad
transcript: FlexiJoint contains glucosamine and chondroitin. Some studies suggest these ingredients may support joint comfort. Talk to your doctor about whether FlexiJoint is right for you. Individual results may vary.
rationale: Properly hedged language ('may support'), directs to physician, includes disclaimer

name: Herbal pain reliever false safety claim
transcript: Tired of ibuprofen side effects? HerbRelief is the all-natural pain solution without the side effects of over-the-counter pain relievers. 100% plant-based, zero stomach irritation guaranteed.
rationale: False safety claim — comparing favorably to OTC drugs without disclosing own side effects (FTC Example 9)

name: CBD pain relief without side effects
transcript: CBDCalm offers natural pain relief without any of the dangerous side effects of prescription painkillers. No addiction risk, no liver damage, just pure plant power.
rationale: Implied drug comparison + absolute safety claim ('no addiction risk') without substantiation

name: Compliant herbal pain product ad
transcript: HerbRelief contains turmeric and willow bark, which have been used traditionally for comfort. This product is not intended to replace medical treatment. Consult your healthcare provider before use.
rationale: No comparative safety claim, traditional use framing, proper disclaimers

name: Sports drink with clinically tested ingredient claim
transcript: PowerFlow contains a clinically tested ingredient proven to improve blood flow by 40% and boost endurance. Used by elite athletes worldwide. Fuel your performance.
rationale: Misleading 'clinically tested' claim — studies on isolated ingredient don't prove product efficacy (FTC Example 18)

name: Pre-workout with clinical research claim
transcript: NitroBoost features ingredients backed by peer-reviewed clinical research. Increase your VO2 max and crush your personal records. The science speaks for itself.
rationale: Implied clinical proof for product when research was on individual ingredients in different dosages

name: Compliant sports nutrition ad
transcript: PowerFlow is formulated with electrolytes and B vitamins to support your active lifestyle. As with any supplement, individual responses may vary. Not a substitute for a balanced diet.
rationale: Structure/function claim ('support active lifestyle') without efficacy promise

name: Heart health juice proven claim
transcript: HeartGuard juice is proven to promote cardiovascular health. Drink one glass daily and reduce your risk of heart disease. Clinically validated formula.
rationale: 'Proven' claim based on single small study (FTC Example 31) — one trial doesn't support 'proven'

name: Omega-3 cardiovascular proven benefit
transcript: OmegaMax is scientifically proven to lower your cholesterol and protect your heart. Over 10,000 satisfied customers can't be wrong. Take control of your heart health today.
rationale: 'Scientifically proven' disease prevention claim for supplement without adequate substantiation

name: Compliant heart-healthy food ad
transcript: HeartGuard juice contains antioxidants from pomegranate. While research on pomegranate and heart health is ongoing, a healthy diet including fruits may contribute to cardiovascular wellness.
rationale: Properly qualified ('research is ongoing', 'may contribute'), no disease claim

name: Weight loss device with specific numbers
transcript: The AbToner 3000 — in just 10 minutes a day for 30 days, you can effortlessly lose two or more inches and 10 pounds from your waist. FDA registered device. Results guaranteed.
rationale: Specific weight loss numbers + 'effortlessly' + misuse of FDA registration as endorsement (FTC Example 48)

name: Weight loss belt infomercial
transcript: SlimBelt vibrating technology melts away belly fat. Lose 3 inches in your first week. No gym, no diet changes needed. Just wear it while watching TV. Thousands of 5-star reviews.
rationale: Specific loss claim + 'no diet/exercise' + passive device efficacy — classic FTC violation pattern

name: Compliant exercise equipment ad
transcript: The AbToner helps you engage your core muscles during a workout. Results depend on consistent use combined with a balanced diet and regular exercise. Consult a fitness professional before starting any program.
rationale: No specific weight loss numbers, requires diet+exercise, proper disclaimers

name: Cholesterol supplement with hedged but misleading language
transcript: Exciting new research suggests CholestAway may help maintain healthy cholesterol levels already within normal range. Promising preliminary studies point to real benefits. Try it today.
rationale: Qualifiers like 'promising' and 'preliminary' provide positive spin that misleads rather than disclaims (FTC Example 12)

name: Brain supplement hypothalamus mechanism claim
transcript: NeuroSlim targets your brain's hypothalamus to naturally signal your body to burn stored fat while you sleep. Patented neuro-receptor technology backed by 15 years of research.
rationale: Pseudo-scientific mechanism claim ('signal hypothalamus to burn fat') — FTC Florida Supplement case

name: Fat-burning coffee with science claims
transcript: BurnBrew coffee activates thermogenesis at the cellular level to accelerate fat oxidation. Peer-reviewed ingredients. Doctor formulated. Lose weight with your morning coffee.
rationale: Pseudo-scientific mechanism + weight loss promise + 'doctor formulated' implying endorsement

name: Compliant metabolism support supplement
transcript: MetaBoost contains green tea extract and caffeine, which some research associates with a modest increase in metabolic rate. This product is not intended for weight loss. A healthy diet and exercise are essential for weight management.
rationale: Modest structure/function claim, explicitly disclaims weight loss, requires diet+exercise

name: Sleep supplement for anxiety without interaction warning
transcript: Can't sleep? MellowNight is your all-natural solution for when life's stresses get you down or you're too anxious to fall asleep. No prescription needed. Non-habit forming. Works the first night.
rationale: Marketed for anxiety/insomnia (drug-like claims) without disclosing dangerous drug interactions (FTC Example 11)

name: Diabetes supplement testimonial with specific numbers
transcript: Listen to what happened to me. The first pill I took, I could feel a difference. My blood sugar went from 549 to 112 in 24 hours. GlucoBalance changed my life. Order yours today.
rationale: Specific blood sugar numbers in testimonial without typicality disclosure or substantiation (FTC Nobetes case 2018)

name: Weight loss testimonial without typicality
transcript: I lost 47 pounds in just 6 weeks using TrimFast. I didn't change anything else about my life. This product is a miracle. If I can do it, so can you.
rationale: Testimonial with specific atypical results + no disclaimer + 'miracle' language + implied anyone can replicate

name: Compliant supplement testimonial
transcript: I've been taking GlucoBalance for three months as part of my overall health program including diet changes and exercise. I've noticed I feel better overall. Results shown are not typical and individual results will vary. Consult your doctor.
rationale: Vague benefit, mentions diet+exercise, explicit typicality disclaimer, doctor referral

name: Diabetes symptom cure testimonial
transcript: I used to have tingling in my arms, dry mouth, and blurry vision every night. After just one week on DiabeCure, all of those symptoms are completely gone. It's like I never had diabetes.
rationale: Testimonial implying product cures diabetes symptoms without typicality disclosure (FTC Nobetes 2018)

name: Influencer supplement promotion without disclosure
transcript: Hey guys, I've been using ImmunoBoost every morning and honestly I haven't been sick in months. Like this stuff actually works. Link in bio if you want to try it. You won't regret it.
rationale: Paid endorsement without #ad disclosure + implied efficacy claim ('actually works') without substantiation

name: Immune system disease prevention claim
transcript: ImmuneShield super-charges your immune system to defeat the common cold, flu, viruses, and even deadly diseases. Pharmaceutical grade ingredients at a fraction of the cost.
rationale: Disease prevention/treatment claims for supplement + 'pharmaceutical grade' implies drug status (FTC Florida case)

name: Vitamin C immune disease shield
transcript: MegaC 5000 creates an impenetrable shield against all viruses and bacteria. Eliminates cold and flu guaranteed or your money back. Why risk getting sick?
rationale: Absolute disease prevention claim ('impenetrable shield', 'eliminates', 'all viruses') — no supplement can make this claim

name: Compliant immune support supplement
transcript: ImmuneShield contains vitamin C and zinc, which support normal immune function. Adequate intake of these nutrients is part of a healthy lifestyle. Not intended to prevent or treat any disease.
rationale: Structure/function claim ('support normal immune function'), proper disclaimer, no disease claims

name: Blood pressure supplement with specific stat
transcript: HyperTone reduces health-related time-off from work by a whopping 97 percent. Lower your blood pressure naturally with our proprietary blend. Results in as little as two weeks.
rationale: Specific unsubstantiated statistic (97%) + disease treatment claim ('lower blood pressure') (FTC Florida case)

name: Compliant blood pressure wellness ad
transcript: HyperTone contains hawthorn berry and CoQ10. Some studies suggest these may support healthy blood pressure already within the normal range. This is not a substitute for prescribed medication. See your doctor.
rationale: Properly qualified ('may support', 'already within normal range'), not a treatment claim, doctor referral

name: Probiotic digestive health with prevalence stat
transcript: Did you know 87% of Americans suffer from digestive issues? DigestPro with patented probiotic strain is clinically proven to eliminate bloating and irregularity within 48 hours.
rationale: Unsubstantiated prevalence statistic + 'clinically proven' + 'eliminate' efficacy claim (FTC Dannon case)

name: Yogurt digestive aid with clinical proof claim
transcript: GutRenew with live active cultures is scientifically proven to solve your digestive problems. Eat one cup daily for regularity. Clinically validated by doctors at leading universities.
rationale: 'Scientifically proven to solve digestive problems' is unsubstantiated disease claim for food product (FTC Dannon)

name: Compliant probiotic ad
transcript: GutRenew contains Lactobacillus cultures that may help maintain digestive balance when consumed as part of a balanced diet. Individual digestive experiences differ. Not intended to treat any condition.
rationale: Structure/function ('maintain digestive balance'), hedged ('may help'), proper disclaimers

name: Weight loss before/after with inadequate disclaimer
transcript: Look at Sarah's transformation! She lost 45 pounds in just 8 weeks with SlimMax. These results are not typical. Your weight loss may not be the same. But Sarah did it, and you can too!
rationale: Fine print disclaimer contradicted by 'you can too' — disclaimer doesn't cure misleading impression (FTC Example 38)

name: Dramatic weight loss testimonial with asterisk
transcript: I went from a size 18 to a size 4 in three months.* (*Results not typical.) FastBurn changed everything for me. Don't wait — start your transformation today.
rationale: Asterisk disclaimer for atypical dramatic results is insufficient — FTC requires prominent expected results disclosure

name: Compliant weight management testimonial
transcript: I've been using SlimMax alongside a 1500 calorie diet and walking 30 minutes daily. Over 6 months, I've gradually lost weight. In a clinical study, average weight loss was 3 pounds over 8 weeks compared to 1 pound for placebo.
rationale: Mentions diet+exercise, gradual timeline, cites actual study averages as typicality disclosure

name: Nobel Prize research misattribution
transcript: BrainMax is formulated based on Nobel Prize-winning neuroscience research. Proven effective by over $5 million in NIH-funded studies. The smartest choice for your brain.
rationale: Misattributing Nobel Prize and NIH research to imply product was proven in those studies (FTC Example 17)

name: Harvard research brain supplement
transcript: Developed from research at Harvard Medical School. CogniPlus is clinically proven to reverse age-related cognitive decline. Restore your mental sharpness in just 14 days.
rationale: Misattributing university research + 'reverse cognitive decline' disease claim + specific timeframe

name: Compliant brain health supplement
transcript: CogniPlus contains DHA and phosphatidylserine, nutrients that play a role in brain function. While some research exists on these nutrients, we make no claims about treating or preventing any condition. Speak with your healthcare provider.
rationale: Describes nutrient role without efficacy claim, explicitly disclaims, references provider

name: Memory software clinically proven
transcript: BrainTrainer is clinically proven to improve your memory, focus, and cognitive performance. Used by executives at Fortune 500 companies. Sharpen your mind in just 5 minutes a day.
rationale: Study tested narrow working memory tasks; ad generalizes to all cognitive performance (FTC Example 32)

name: Compliant brain training app
transcript: BrainTrainer offers puzzles and exercises designed to challenge your working memory. While enjoyable, no app can guarantee cognitive improvement. Think of it as a gym for your brain — results depend on consistent practice.
rationale: No efficacy claim, honest framing ('no app can guarantee'), analogy without promise

name: Crypto guaranteed returns
transcript: CryptoWealth AI guarantees 500% returns in 30 days. Zero risk — our algorithm never loses. Join 50,000 members already earning passive income. Limited spots available, act now.
rationale: Guaranteed returns + zero risk + specific ROI + urgency scarcity — violates financial advertising rules on all platforms

name: Forex trading bot guaranteed income
transcript: ForexMaster bot makes you money while you sleep. Guaranteed minimum $500 per day. No experience needed, our AI does everything. Join the financial freedom revolution.
rationale: Guaranteed daily income + no risk/effort claims + implied algorithmic certainty — deceptive financial claim

name: Investment course with earnings claims
transcript: My students are making $10,000 a month following my system. This exact blueprint took me from broke to millionaire in 18 months. Enroll today and change your financial future.
rationale: Specific earnings claims without typicality disclosure or 'results not typical' — implies these are common outcomes

name: Compliant investment education ad
transcript: Learn the fundamentals of investing with our educational course. Trading involves substantial risk of loss and is not suitable for all investors. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Only invest what you can afford to lose.
rationale: Educational framing, prominent risk disclosure, no earnings claims, proper disclaimers

name: Fake scarcity supplement offer
transcript: WARNING: Due to overwhelming demand, we only have 47 bottles left. This price won't last — after midnight tonight it goes back to $89.99. Order in the next 15 minutes and get free shipping.
rationale: Fabricated scarcity + time pressure — if this offer recurs regularly, 'tonight only' is deceptive urgency

name: Limited time offer always running
transcript: Flash sale! 70% off everything. Today only! This is your last chance to save big. Once it's gone, it's gone forever. Don't miss out on this once-in-a-lifetime deal.
rationale: If this 'today only' sale runs repeatedly, it's deceptive urgency — 'once-in-a-lifetime' implies unique event

name: Compliant limited promotion
transcript: We're offering 20% off through the end of this month as part of our summer promotion. After July 31st, regular pricing resumes. No pressure — shop when you're ready.
rationale: Specific end date, no false scarcity, no psychological pressure language

name: Lifestyle influencer undisclosed promotion
transcript: Good morning everyone! Starting my day with this amazing green smoothie from VitaGreens. Honestly the best thing I've added to my routine this year. The energy is unreal. Swipe up to get yours!
rationale: Paid promotion framed as organic endorsement without #ad or material connection disclosure — FTC Endorsement Guides

name: Compliant influencer promotion
transcript: Ad. VitaGreens sent me this to try and I've been enjoying it in my morning routine. I can't make any health claims about it, but I like the taste. If you're interested, my affiliate link is in the description.
rationale: Clear 'Ad' disclosure at start, acknowledges gifted product, no efficacy claims, transparent affiliate relationship
